subject.title: fix(reef): add timeout and bounded JSON reads to relay transport

question: Should Reef relay HTTP requests use a fixed 15-second deadline that also limits reading an otherwise healthy response body?
rationale: This is an intentional availability-versus-slow-relay compatibility contract, not a mechanical correctness choice settled by the tests.

options.title: Accept the 15-second contract
options.body: Keep the fixed deadline, rebase the branch, and require current-head proof that both header and body stalls abort while recovery still works.

options.title: Use an established Reef timeout source
options.body: If Reef already has an owner-approved timeout policy or configuration surface, resolve the request deadline from that contract instead of introducing a new fixed value.

options.title: Pause pending owner policy
options.body: Do not merge until the expected latency envelope for relay uploads, pulls, and response reads is defined.

recommendation.title: Accept the 15-second contract
recommendation.body: Keep the fixed deadline, rebase the branch, and require current-head proof that both header and body stalls abort while recovery still works.

likelyOwner.reason: The assignee authored the latest branch change that establishes the whole-response timeout behavior.
